description: Regression catalog for head2phones preparation edge cases. Tests load this file directly; keep cases small, specific, and tied to an observed or plausible data-prep failure.

cases.input: The Loadstone Rock was drawing him.
cases.note: Archaic spelling in A Tale of Two Cities must use the lodestone pronunciation, not a fallback guess.
Link-grammar context should pick CMUdict's saint candidate for St. before a proper name.
Street/address contexts should keep CMUdict's street candidate for St.

cases.input: Dr. Smith went home. Then he slept.
cases.note: Title abbreviations must not split the head at the abbreviation period.

cases.input: No. 5 was missing from the list. Then it appeared.
cases.note: No. before a digit is an abbreviation, not a sentence boundary.
cases.expected_head: No. 5 was missing from the list.

cases.input: Dr. Smith saw No. 5 at 3.14 p.m. before leaving.
cases.note: Decimals and dotted time abbreviations should not create false head boundaries.
cases.expected_head: Dr. Smith saw No. 5 at 3.14 p.m. before leaving.

cases.input: After the meeting, Rep. Susan Smith (D. NY.) said she didn't know what the meeting was about.
cases.note: Political title, party, and state abbreviations should not split before the sentence end.
cases.expected_head: After the meeting, Rep. Susan Smith (D. NY.) said she didn't know what the meeting was about.

cases.note: Incomplete streaming prefixes should train as <NO_HEAD> instead of being flushed early.
At end of text, title-like fragments are speakable heads for flush examples.
If an earlier model or naive splitter emitted `Who shot John F.` too early, the next buffer should be able to signal a low-confidence repair and tell the caller how far back to roll.
